established: Recipe choice ambiguity is a known phenomenon in established measurement frameworks: code coverage (line/branch/path), information retrieval (micro/macro/weighted averaging of precision/recall/F1), web analytics. IR evidence strongest. (EXP-INTEL-35280397316 result.json M1-M3, audit.json B1)

Recipe choice ambiguity additionally documented in psychometrics (Kane & Case 2003 mixed-format composite weighting; PMC5978518 composite score construction from multiple measures) and econometrics (OECD 2008 Handbook arithmetic vs geometric vs weighted product for composite indicators; Munda 2005 social choice theory for aggregation rule selection). Non-systematic synthesis ceiling — not systematic review. (EXP-INTEL-35290611333 result.json M1-M2, audit.json B1_POSITIVE_CONTROL_PC1 recomputed min 5-6 distinct ≥2)

OECD/COINr sensitivity analysis framework provides principled MIXED-outcome handling method: systematically vary aggregation methods and weights, quantify ranking stability via dominance pairs and confidence intervals, report robustness bounds rather than choosing one recipe. Non-systematic synthesis ceiling, interpretive analogy to SPIDER. (EXP-INTEL-35290611333 result.json M4 strong=1, audit.json B2_POSITIVE_CONTROL_PC2)

Principled resolution methods exist across fields: (1) recipe-as-question-answer binding, (2) sensitivity reporting, (3) micro/macro/weighted framework, (4) OECD sensitivity analysis.
